scan.summary: This is the company's internal Emergency Action Plan for the Portland facility describing what employees must do during a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake, or other emergency. The plan covers 42 employees across warehouse, laboratory, and office areas and specifies alarm signals, evacuation routes, assembly points, rescue and medical procedures, and employee training responsibilities.
scan.freshness_note: Document is from February 2021, now over five years old. The plan is required to be reviewed annually per 29 CFR 1910.38(f) and OAR 437-002-0042, and no evidence is provided that it has been reviewed or updated since the revision date. An updated version should be obtained.

gaps.title: Missing specific contact name or job title for plan coordination
gaps.description: The plan mentions 'the incident coordinator at the assembly point' but does not name any individual or provide the job title of the person responsible for coordinating emergency response and providing information about plan duties. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(6) requires the name or job title of every employee who may be contacted by employees who need more information about the plan.
gaps.fix: Add to the plan the name and/or job title of the incident coordinator and any other key emergency personnel (e.g., emergency coordinator, safety manager) who employees can contact for questions about the plan or their duties.
gaps.locator: Section 1 (Purpose and scope) or new section on emergency contacts
gaps.quote: Any person unaccounted for is reported at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point

gaps.title: Missing documentation of employee notification procedures for plan review
gaps.description: The plan states that 'the plan is reviewed with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change,' but does not document how this review is conducted, recorded, or communicated. The standard requires review at initial assignment, when duties change, and when the plan changes. No evidence is shown that reviews have been completed and documented.
gaps.fix: Add procedures for documenting employee review of the emergency action plan. Include a statement that a sign-in sheet or training record is maintained showing who has been trained on the plan and when. Ensure training logs are kept and updated whenever the plan is revised.
gaps.quote: The plan is reviewed with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.

gaps.title: No evidence of plan update or review since February 2021
gaps.description: The document is dated 'Revised February 2021' but provides no evidence of a January review as stated in the plan. The regulation 29 CFR 1910.38(f) and OAR 437-002-0042(5) require the plan to be reviewed with all employees when it is changed. No record is provided showing whether the plan has been reviewed in the past 5+ years or whether any updates have been made to reflect changes in personnel, building layout, or contact information.
gaps.fix: Obtain the most current version of the Emergency Action Plan and provide evidence (such as dated sign-in sheets, meeting minutes, or revision records) that the plan has been reviewed annually with all employees as required. Update Appendix B (floor warden and first-aid responder roster) to confirm current personnel assignments.
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

gaps.title: Missing specification of drill frequency and records
gaps.description: The plan states 'Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn' but provides no evidence of completed drills, no records of dates drills were conducted, and no documentation of attendance or corrective actions taken after drills. 29 CFR 1910.38 requires that training be documented and that the plan's effectiveness be demonstrated through drills.
gaps.fix: Maintain a log of all evacuation drills conducted, including date, time, department(s) participating, number of employees evacuated, time to complete evacuation, and any issues or corrective actions identified. Provide this log as evidence of compliance.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(e) and (f); industry practice implies annual minimum
gaps.locator: Section 4 (Accounting for employees after evacuation) and Section 6 (Training and review)
gaps.quote: Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.

gaps.title: No evidence of documented first-aid responder and floor warden training records
gaps.description: Section 6 states that 'Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually' but no training records, dates, or attendance lists are provided in the document. Appendix B is referenced as containing the roster but is not included in the materials provided. No evidence of CPR, first-aid certification, or evacuation warden training is shown.
gaps.fix: Provide training records for all designated floor wardens and first-aid responders showing the date of training, trainer name, and certification status. For first-aid responders, provide evidence of current first-aid and CPR certification. Ensure records are maintained and updated when personnel change or recertification is needed.
gaps.locator: Section 5 (Rescue and medical duties) and Section 6 (Training and review)
gaps.quote: Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually.

gaps.title: Emergency shower and eyewash location not explicitly mapped or tested
gaps.description: The plan states that 'An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely' but the plan does not confirm that these fixtures exist, are operational, or provide specific location details in the evacuation maps (Appendix A).
gaps.fix: Confirm in the plan that emergency shower and eyewash stations exist at the loading dock and are functional. Include testing records showing that these stations are inspected and tested at least quarterly per ANSI Z535.1. Add the location to Appendix A (evacuation maps).
gaps.citation: ANSI Z535.1 and industry best practice; referenced in 29 CFR 1910.1450 (occupational exposure to hazardous chemicals in laboratories)
gaps.quote: An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely

gaps.title: Visitor orientation procedures not documented
gaps.description: The plan states the plan 'applies to...contractors and visitors while on site' but does not specify the procedures for orienting visitors and contractors to evacuation routes, assembly points, or hazards upon arrival at the facility.
gaps.fix: Add a new section or subsection specifying that all visitors and contractors must be given a brief orientation covering: (1) location of evacuation map for their area; (2) assembly point location and distance; (3) alarm signals and their meanings; and (4) that they must follow the directions of facility employees and floor wardens. Document this orientation in a visitor log.
gaps.quote: It applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site.

gaps.title: Alarm system maintenance and test records not documented
gaps.description: Section 2 states 'The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead' but does not specify where test records are maintained or provide evidence of completed tests. 29 CFR 1910.165 requires the alarm system to be tested, and records should be available for inspection.
gaps.fix: Maintain a log or testing schedule showing: (1) date of each monthly alarm test; (2) name of person conducting the test; (3) all areas tested (warehouse, laboratory, loading dock, offices); (4) whether the alarm functioned correctly in all locations; and (5) any maintenance or repairs performed. Provide evidence of this log.
gaps.quote: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead.

gaps.title: Mechanical room ventilation shutdown procedure not detailed
gaps.description: Section 3 mentions that 'the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel' during shelter-in-place scenarios but provides no step-by-step instructions, lock-out/tag-out procedures, or documentation that the facilities lead has been trained and certified to perform this safety-critical task.
gaps.fix: Add detailed written procedures for ventilation shutdown, including: (1) the specific steps to take; (2) location of the mechanical room; (3) identification of all controls to be operated; (4) safety precautions (e.g., LOTO if applicable); and (5) confirmation that the facilities lead has been trained, tested, and documented as competent to perform this task under emergency conditions.
gaps.citation: Best practice under 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(3) (procedures for critical equipment shutdown)
gaps.quote: the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel

expected_missing.title: Fire Prevention Plan
expected_missing.why: Companies subject to emergency action plan requirements typically also have a fire prevention plan (29 CFR 1910.39), which would detail fire hazards, equipment maintenance, and employee roles in preventing fires.
expected_missing.basis: standard OSHA requirement for facilities handling chemicals or with fire alarm systems

expected_missing.title: Chemical inventory list and SDSs
expected_missing.why: A chemical manufacturing facility should maintain Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for all hazardous chemicals on site, as required by the Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200).

expected_missing.title: Material Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) accessibility log
expected_missing.why: The plan references bringing 'the SDS for the product' to responders but does not document where SDSs are stored, how they are accessed, or that they are available in the assembly point or medical treatment area.
expected_missing.basis: Emergency response best practice; required by 29 CFR 1910.1200

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the document's structure and primary content. The plan addresses the six minimum elements of 29 CFR 1910.38(c) and is written clearly with specific procedures for the Portland facility. However, confidence is reduced regarding current applicability because: (1) the plan is dated February 2021 (over 5 years old) and should have been reviewed and updated annually; (2) no evidence is provided of completed drills, training records, or roster updates; (3) appendices (evacuation maps and warden roster) are referenced but not provided; (4) the plan does not name the incident coordinator or emergency contact personnel, a specific gap under 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(6). The regulatory trigger for requiring this EAP is not explicitly stated in the document—it is inferred that a chemical manufacturing operation with 42 employees falls under a standard requiring an EAP (likely 29 CFR 1910.119, Process Safety Management, if the facility handles highly hazardous chemicals, or a lower-hazard standard if not). Oregon follows federal OSHA standards under OAR 437-002-0042, which mirrors 29 CFR 1910.38. No statement was found in the document itself that definitively triggers the EAP requirement.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
